title: Why You Should Never Share Social Media With Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: After a reader alerted him to teachers sharing personal social media handles with students, Linsin spent several days confirming with contacts around the country and reports the practice is happening far more widely than he expected. His central claim is that this is straightforwardly inappropriate regardless of the teacher's intent — whether it's framed as sharing music, art, or a side project, he calls it an "ego play" that damages a teacher's authority and professional standing. He backs the argument with a list of documented harms associated with social media use — anxiety, addiction, cyberbullying, depression, lower attention span, and worse academic outcomes — arguing that teachers who share accounts are implicitly endorsing exposure to those risks. The concrete recommendation for anyone who has already shared a handle is immediate: switch the account to private or start an entirely new one. He closes with an unusually sharp tone for the site, framing protection of student welfare as an obligation he'll defend without apology, and encourages readers to report colleagues who engage in the practice to administrators.
points: Linsin spent days confirming with contacts nationwide that teacher-student social media sharing is happening far more widely than expected.
Documented harms cited include anxiety, addiction, cyberbullying, depression, and worse academic outcomes.
Even seemingly innocent reasons for sharing a handle — music, art, a side project — are called an inappropriate "ego play."
Teachers who have already shared a handle are advised to immediately make it private or start a new account.
quotes: Evidently, there are teachers sharing their personal social-media pages with students.
For what possible innocent reason would any teacher do this? I can’t think of any.
Why would a teacher proactively play a part in, and all but give their blessing to, something that the overwhelming research shows is bad for students?
I’ve written over 800 articles for SCM and try never to allow any perception of anger to seep into my words. I can’t do it this time.
A source told me that at her school nearly every teacher does this. They even follow their students back.
